# Projections

`jb3_project()` projects the stock under constant $F/F_{MSY}$ scenarios (`fmsy`,
the default: 0, 0.5, 0.75, 1 and 1.25 $F_{MSY}$) or constant catch (`catch`),
from the NUTS draws or from MVN draws at the mode (generated if the fit has
none), with process error (and its AR(1) persistence and the lag). F-based
scenarios apply $F = f \times F_{MSY}$ draw by draw, so they remain defined
when a draw is depleted; constant catches are capped at 95% of the biomass.

```{r proj}
pj <- jb3_project(fit, fmsy = c(0, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.25), nyears = 10)
pj$scenarios
```

Process error in the projection years follows the fitted model. With the
default `procerr = "ar1"`, each draw continues its AR(1) process from its last
estimated deviation, $d_{t+1} = \rho d_t + \varepsilon_t$ with
$\varepsilon_t \sim N(0, \sigma^2(1-\rho^2))$, so the persistence carries into
the forecast and the marginal SD stays $\sigma$ (with $\rho = 0$ this is the iid
sampling of JABBA's `fw_jabba()`). `procerr = "mean"` uses only the conditional
mean $\rho^h d_T$ and `"none"` deterministic production. Projection tables
report the risk $P(B < B_{lim})$ with $B_{lim} = 0.3 B_{MSY}$ by default.

```{r proj-plot, fig.height = 6}
jbplot_projection(pj)
```

`jbplot_projection()` draws $B_{MSY}$ and $F_{MSY}$ (green), MSY on the catch
panel, a biomass threshold `bthr` (orange, default $0.5 B_{MSY}$) and limit
`blim` (red, default $0.3 B_{MSY}$). A name sets the label, e.g.
`bthr = c(Bpa = 0.5)` (ICES) or `bthr = c(MSST = 1 - M)` (U.S.), `NULL` omits
one, and `extra` adds further lines, e.g. `extra = c(Flim = 1.3)`:

```{r proj-plot-refpts, fig.height = 6}
jbplot_projection(pj, bthr = c(MSST = 1 - 0.2), blim = NULL, extra = c(Flim = 1.3))
```

## Projections on the advice plot

`jbplot_advice(fit, proj = )` appends the projection scenarios (dashed) to the
assessment advice plot:

```{r proj-advice, fig.height = 7, fig.width = 7}
jbplot_advice(fit, proj = pj)
```

## Projection tables

`jb3_projtable()` gives a catch options table in the style of an ICES advice
sheet: $F/F_{MSY}$, $F$ and the catch in the first projection year, the median
$B/B_{MSY}$ in selected years with the change relative to the terminal year,
and the probabilities of $B \ge B_{MSY}$, $F \le F_{MSY}$ and of the Kobe
green quadrant.

```{r proj-tab}
knitr::kable(jb3_projtable(pj, years = c(2018, 2022, 2027)))
```

`jb3_kobematrix()` is the Kobe II strategy matrix (ICCAT): the probability of
being in the green quadrant by scenario and year (`what = "B"` or `"F"` for
one reference point only).

```{r proj-k2sm}
knitr::kable(jb3_kobematrix(pj))
```

## Kobe II strategy matrices

The Kobe II strategy matrix (K2SM) gives, by management option (rows) and
projection year (columns), the probability of meeting reference points.
`jb3_kobematrix()` computes it from any projection, in the ICCAT format by
default; `jb3_kobematrix_iotc()`, `jb3_kobematrix_gfcm()` and
`jb3_kobematrix_ices()` give the IOTC, GFCM and ICES formats, and
`jbplot_kobematrix()` plots them, shaded in grey as in the report tables
(`colours = "grey"`, default) or red to green (`colours = "kobe"`). All
scenarios of a projection share the same process-error draws, so intermediate
years are identical across rows and the probabilities change monotonically
with the option. Each matrix below is computed from the projection plotted
just before it.

### Catch (TAC) options: ICCAT and IOTC

Constant catches of 60-130% of the catch in the last assessment year, after
one intermediate year at the status quo catch (`imp.years = 1`):

```{r k2sm-tac}
cref <- tail(fit$data$catch, 1)
pt <- jb3_project(fit, catch = round(cref*seq(0.6, 1.3, 0.1), -2), nyears = 10, imp.years = 1)
```

```{r k2sm-tac-plot, fig.height = 7, fig.width = 8}
jbplot_projection(pt)
```

The ICCAT matrices (a) $P(F < F_{MSY})$, (b) $P(B > B_{MSY})$ and (c) both
(the green Kobe quadrant):

```{r k2sm-iccat}
k2 <- jb3_kobematrix(pt, what = "all", percent = TRUE)
k2
```

```{r k2sm-iccat-plot, fig.height = 8, fig.width = 8}
jbplot_kobematrix(pt)
```

`what = "green"` (default), `"B"` or `"F"` returns one matrix, and
`percent = FALSE` proportions. Projections from several models (e.g.
alternative production functions, or runs with and without the lag) are
combined into one matrix with equal or given `weights`, as the ICCAT combined
matrices of two base cases:

```{r k2sm-comb, eval = FALSE}
jb3_kobematrix(list(Fox = pt.fox, Schaefer = pt.sch), what = "all", percent = TRUE)
```

The IOTC format from the same projection: catch options relative to the
reference catch, and the probability (%) of violating the MSY-based reference
points, $P(B < B_{MSY})$ and $P(F > F_{MSY})$, and the limit reference points,
$P(B < B_{lim})$ and $P(F > F_{lim})$ (defaults $B_{lim} = 0.5 B_{MSY}$,
$F_{lim} = 1.3 F_{MSY}$; `blim`, `flim`), 3 and 10 years after the last
assessment year (`years`):

```{r k2sm-iotc}
kio <- jb3_kobematrix_iotc(pt, ref.catch = cref)
kio
```

```{r k2sm-iotc-plot, fig.height = 4.5, fig.width = 10}
jbplot_kobematrix(kio, colours = "kobe")
```

### F options: GFCM and ICES

GFCM and ICES advice is usually based on F options. Named scenarios
(`scenarios` in `jb3_project()`) are reported in the order and with the names
given; each is one named value, with `Catch`, `Fmsy` (F/F~MSY~), `F` (harvest
rate), `Fsq` or `Csq` (multipliers of the status quo).

F options relative to $F_{MSY}$ (`Fmsy = 0.8`) apply $F = 0.8 F_{MSY}$ draw by
draw, so $P(F < F_{MSY})$ is 0 or 100%. As in the GFCM and ICES forecasts
(e.g. SPiCT `add.man.scenario(fabs = )`), the F options are therefore set as
absolute harvest rates from the point estimates of $F_{MSY}$ and the current F
(mean of the last three years): $F = 0$, 0.5-2 $F_{tgt}$ ($F_{tgt} = F_{MSY}$),
$F_{cur}$, and the precautionary $F_{MSY}$ PA (35th percentile of $F_{MSY}$):

```{r k2sm-fopt}
rp <- fit$refpts
Fmsy <- rp["Fmsy", "est"]
Fcur <- mean(tail(fit$ts$est[fit$ts$quantity == "F"], 3))
Fmsy.pa <- exp(qnorm(0.35, log(Fmsy), rp["Fmsy", "se.log"]))
mult <- c(0, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.25, 1.5, 2)
fopt <- c(setNames(lapply(mult, function(m) c(F = m*Fmsy)),
                   c("F0", "0.5Ftgt", "0.75Ftgt", "Ftgt", "1.25Ftgt", "1.5Ftgt", "2Ftgt")),
          list(Fcur = c(F = Fcur), "Fmsy PA" = c(F = Fmsy.pa)))
pf <- jb3_project(fit, scenarios = fopt, nyears = 10, imp.years = 1)
```

```{r k2sm-fopt-plot, fig.height = 7, fig.width = 8}
jbplot_projection(pf)
```

With absolute F options, $P(F < F_{MSY})$ is the probability that the option
is below the uncertain $F_{MSY}$: 50% for $F_{tgt}$, so the joint probability
of the green quadrant cannot exceed 50% at $F_{tgt}$, even where the median
biomass is above $B_{MSY}$.

`jb3_kobematrix_gfcm()` gives the three matrices of the GFCM advice summary
sheet: (a) $P(F < F_{tgt}$ and $B > B_{tgt})$, (b) $P(B > B_{thr})$ and (c) the
risk $P(B < B_{lim})$, with $B_{tgt} = B_{MSY}$, $F_{tgt} = F_{MSY}$,
$B_{thr} = 0.5 B_{MSY}$ and $B_{lim} = 0.3 B_{MSY}$ by default (`btgt`,
`ftgt`, `bthr`, `blim`):

```{r k2sm-gfcm}
kg <- jb3_kobematrix_gfcm(pf)
kg
```

Probabilities are shaded darker (greener) the higher they are, risks darker
(redder) the higher the risk, on finer classes (`risk.breaks`):

```{r k2sm-gfcm-plot, fig.height = 9, fig.width = 8}
jbplot_kobematrix(kg, colours = "kobe")
```

For ICES-type advice, `jb3_kobematrix_ices()` gives (a)
$P(F < F_{MSY}$ and $B > B_{pa})$ and (b) the risk $P(B < B_{lim})$, to compare
with the ICES 5% threshold, with the SPM proxies $B_{pa} = 0.5 B_{MSY}$ and
$B_{lim} = 0.3 B_{MSY}$ (`bpa`, `blim`):

```{r k2sm-ices, eval = FALSE}
jb3_kobematrix_ices(pf)
```

Other combinations follow from `jb3_kobematrix()` with `bref` and `fref`
(multiples of $B_{MSY}$ and $F_{MSY}$, optionally named; `NULL` drops one) and
`risk = TRUE` for the complement, e.g.
`jb3_kobematrix(pf, what = "all", bref = c(Btrigger = 0.5))`.

## Short-term advice with a hockey-stick HCR

Short-term advice under a harvest control rule (as in the GFCM Type 1
management procedure with JABBA's `fw_jabba_ctrl()` and `jb_hockeystick()`)
takes three steps: a forecast with intermediate years at the status quo catch
followed by $F_{tgt}$, the hockey-stick rule applied to $B/B_{MSY}$ in the first
implementation (TAC) year to obtain the advised $F_{adv}$, and the forecast of
the management options.

Forecast controls (`jb3_fwd()`, as `fw_jabba_ctrl()`) are data frames with one
row per year and `quant` `"Catch"`, `"Fmsy"` (F/F~MSY~), `"F"`, `"Csq"`,
`"Fsq"` or `"HCR"`; here two intermediate years at the status quo catch (mean
of the last three years) and two TAC years:

```{r hcr-ctrl}
y0  <- max(fit$years)
yrs <- y0 + 1:4
csq <- mean(tail(fit$data$catch, 3))
fsq <- mean(tail(fit$ts$est[fit$ts$quantity == "F/Fmsy"], 3))
ctrl <- function(v, q) data.frame(year = yrs, value = c(csq, csq, v, v), quant = c("Catch", "Catch", q, q))
ctrl(1, "Fmsy")
```

`jb3_hcr()` evaluates the rule ($F/F_{MSY} = F_{tgt}$ above $B_{trigger}$,
decreasing linearly below) on $B/B_{MSY}$ in the TAC year of the $F_{tgt}$
forecast. Bigeye is well above the GFCM default $B_{trigger} = 0.5 B_{MSY}$,
where the rule hardly changes F; to illustrate the rule, the example uses
$B_{trigger} = 0.8 B_{MSY}$:

```{r hcr-fadv}
hcr <- jb3_hcr(jb3_fwd(fit, list(Ftgt = ctrl(1, "Fmsy"))), ftgt = 1, btrigger = 0.8, blim = 0.3)
hcr
```

```{r hcr-plot, fig.height = 4.5, fig.width = 6, fig.cap = "Hockey-stick HCR (black line: F/Fmsy against B/Bmsy) with Blim, Btrigger and Bmsy. The blue density is the projected B/Bmsy at the start of the TAC year: each draw is projected from its terminal-year estimate through the intermediate years at the status quo catch, with process error, so the distribution is wider than the current-state posterior. The point is its median and the horizontal bar its 90% interval, drawn at the height of the advised F (F_adv, precautionary: the rule averaged over all draws)."}
jbplot_hcr(hcr)
```

The distribution in the plot is not the current state: it is $B/B_{MSY}$ at the
start of the TAC year, projected from each draw's terminal-year estimate
through the intermediate years, and so includes their process error. The rule
can be evaluated in another forecast year with `year`, e.g.
`jb3_hcr(fwd, year = y0 + 1)` for the year after the assessment.

### Why $F_{adv}$ is below $F_{tgt}$ when the median is above $B_{trigger}$

`jb3_hcr()` offers two ways of turning the uncertain $B/B_{MSY}$ into one
advised F:

- **Deterministic** (`uncertainty = FALSE`, `Fadv.det`): the rule is applied
  once, to the median $B/B_{MSY}$. Here the median is above $B_{trigger}$, so
  $F_{adv} = F_{tgt}$.
- **Precautionary** (`uncertainty = TRUE`, the default, `Fadv.pa`; as JABBA's
  `jb_hockeystick(uncertainty = TRUE)`): the rule is applied to every draw, and
  the advised F is the mean of the resulting F values,
  $F_{adv} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_i HCR(B_i/B_{MSY})$. This is an expectation over the
  draws, not a fractile of $B/B_{MSY}$.

Draws above $B_{trigger}$ get $F_{tgt}$; draws below it get a reduced F,
$F_{tgt} (B_i/B_{MSY})/B_{trigger}$ (with `bclose = 0`). Because the rule is
capped at $F_{tgt}$, uncertainty can only pull the mean down: the precautionary
$F_{adv}$ is never above the deterministic one, and it drops below $F_{tgt}$ as
soon as a share of the draws falls below $B_{trigger}$, even when the median is
above it. The decomposition:

```{r hcr-explain}
bt <- 0.8
f.i <- JABBA3:::.hockey(hcr$b, ftgt = 1, btrigger = bt, bclose = 0, fmin = 0.001)   # F/Fmsy for each draw
below <- hcr$b < bt
data.frame(`median B/Bmsy` = median(hcr$b),
           `P(B < Btrigger)` = mean(below),
           `mean F, draws below` = mean(f.i[below]),
           `mean F, draws above` = mean(f.i[!below]),
           `Fadv.det` = hcr$Fadv.det,
           `Fadv.pa` = hcr$Fadv.pa, check.names = FALSE)
```

so $F_{adv} = P(B < B_{trigger}) \times \bar F_{below} + (1 - P(B < B_{trigger})) \times F_{tgt}$.
The wider the distribution of $B/B_{MSY}$ in the TAC year (larger estimation
uncertainty, process error, longer intermediate period), the larger the
precautionary reduction. With $B_{trigger} = 0.5 B_{MSY}$ only a few draws are
below the trigger and $F_{adv}$ stays close to $F_{tgt}$
(`jb3_hcr(..., btrigger = 0.5)$Fadv`).

### Management options

The options with $F_{adv}$, $F_{tgt}$, $F_{sq}$, $C_{sq}$ and $F = 0$ in the TAC
years, with $B_{trigger}$ marked on the biomass panel:

```{r hcr-stf, fig.height = 7, fig.width = 8}
fc <- list(Fadv = ctrl(hcr$Fadv, "Fmsy"), Ftgt = ctrl(1, "Fmsy"), Fsq = ctrl(fsq, "Fmsy"),
           Csq = ctrl(csq, "Catch"), F0 = ctrl(0, "Fmsy"))
stf <- jb3_fwd(fit, fc)
jbplot_projection(stf, bthr = c(Btrigger = bt))
```

`jb3_fwdtable()` summarises the fishing opportunities in the GFCM format (as
`FLRef::fwd2type1()`): the catch and $F/F_{tgt}$ in the TAC year, the biomass
at the start of the following year, its change, and the probabilities of
being above $B_{lim}$, $B_{pa}$ (here $B_{trigger}$, `bthr`) and $B_{tgt}$:

```{r hcr-table}
knitr::kable(jb3_fwdtable(stf, bthr = bt))
```

Alternatively, `quant = "HCR"` applies the rule draw by draw in every
projection year (`value` = $F_{tgt}$, rule settings in `hcr`), e.g. for a
medium-term projection under the rule:

```{r hcr-drawwise, eval = FALSE}
hcr.ctrl <- data.frame(year = y0 + 1:10, value = c(csq, csq, rep(1, 8)),
                       quant = c("Catch", "Catch", rep("HCR", 8)))
pm <- jb3_fwd(fit, list(HCR = hcr.ctrl), hcr = list(btrigger = bt))
jbplot_projection(pm, bthr = c(Btrigger = bt))
```

For a weighted ensemble, pass a `jb3_ensemble()` instead of the single fit;
the steps are the same.

Constant catch scenarios remain available, e.g. for TAC options:

```{r proj-c, fig.height = 6}
pc <- jb3_project(rec, catch = c(60000, 70000, 80000), nyears = 10)
knitr::kable(jb3_projtable(pc)[, 1:9])
```
